identity.title: SpatioLM: Towards General Physical Spatial Intelligence in Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: Improve visual spatial reasoning and physical spatial intelligence in vision-language models while preserving general-purpose capabilities.

gap.claim: Existing approaches commonly rely on extra 3D priors or external spatial encoders, adding complexity and reportedly degrading general capabilities after spatial fine-tuning.

contributions.claim: A parameter-efficient SpatioLM that enhances spatial intelligence without extra 3D prior inputs or third-party spatial encoders.
A plug-and-play, non-invasive spatio-vision module intended to elicit spatial knowledge already inherent in VLMs.
Use of pseudo depth and camera information as supervision to guide learning of physically coherent representations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their use of pseudo depth and camera information as an innovative form of supervision for physical spatial representation learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant improvements across diverse spatial perception and understanding tasks, while effectively limiting degradation of general capabilities.
The authors report a score of 71.6 on VSI-Bench and identify the model as the first to surpass 70.
The authors report competitive performance after transfer to embodied manipulation tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: VLMs perform well on commonsense reasoning but struggle with visual spatial reasoning.
Existing solutions add 3D priors or external spatial encoders, increasing complexity and reportedly harming general capabilities after spatial fine-tuning.
SpatioLM combines a parameter-efficient design with a non-invasive spatio-vision module and pseudo depth/camera supervision.
The authors report gains across spatial tasks, limited general-capability degradation, a 71.6 VSI-Bench score, and competitive embodied-manipulation transfer.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a targeted spatial module and physically oriented supervision with a preservation goal for general capabilities, then reports both spatial-task and transfer results.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests framing a specialized capability method around both the target gain and the collateral capability it aims to protect.
lessons.application: State the added module, supervision signal, target capability, and preservation objective together, then report evidence for each objective separately.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed system has no meaningful capability-preservation constraint or no evidence relevant to transfer.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baselines, dataset protocols, statistical variability, or how general-capability degradation was measured.
The conditions and metrics underlying the embodied-manipulation transfer claim are not given.
The claimed first-to-surpass-70 status on VSI-Bench is author-reported and not independently verified here.
